name: Lane Ends
spec: yellow diamond with two black lines where the right one tapers into the left
meaning: The right lane ends ahead; merge left early.

snippets.back: Broken white splits same-direction lanes; oversized broken lines warn of lane ends, heed exit and merge signs; yield triangles mark stop-or-yield points.
At a zipper merge where two lanes become one, use both lanes equally until just before the closure, then take turns into the open lane; drivers who wait until the lane ends are doing it right.

Warning signs alert drivers to two-way traffic ahead, merging traffic, right-lane reductions, upcoming roundabouts, divided highways ahead, and divided highway ends—where the divided roadway ends three hundred fifty to five hundred feet ahead before two-way traffic resumes.

Most warning signs are yellow diamonds carrying a black border and black symbols or words, and the examples pictured include divided highway, divided highway ends, hill, slippery when wet, pedestrian crossing, and lane ends or road narrows.
A Lane Ends or Merge Left sign warns that two lanes become one and that merging traffic must yield.
At a lane reduction, merge early if traffic is light; in dense slow traffic use both lanes to the merge point and alternate joining there.
Other warning signs tell you that lanes or roads are changing: a lane ends and you merge left, two roads merge, the road divides ahead, or a divided road ends ahead.
A Lane Ends Merge Left sign means the right lane is ending, so merge left and yield to traffic already in the left lane.

result.correction: A Lane Ends Merge Left sign means the right lane is ending, so merge left and yield to traffic already in the left lane; at a zipper merge use both lanes equally until just before the closure, then take turns into the open lane - in dense slow traffic use both lanes to the merge point and alternate joining there, merge early only if traffic is light.
